macro.headline: Indices recover but breadth narrows as defensives and small-caps lead.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY closed at 737.66, up 1.19% on the day but still down 0.9% over five sessions and 1.99% over the past month. SPY and QQQ both sit above their 50-day and 200-day moving averages but with MACD below signal (SPY hist -2.11, QQQ -3.54) and RSIs sitting flat near 50 — a recovery bounce, not a trend reset. VIX is 18.21, up 5.4% over five days and 15.7% over twenty-one — elevated but not panicked. The Dow (+2.84% over 21d, RSI 63) and Russell 2000 are the relative leaders, while Nasdaq is down 4.8% over 21d. The dollar is firm (DXY RSI 66.6, +2.16% in 21d), and gold (-10.3% in 21d, RSI 34) and silver (-23% in 21d, RSI 30) are getting hit hard — the validated DXY-strength-to-metals headwind is firing in textbook fashion. Oil is down 20.7% in 21d on RSI 30, and the 10y-2y spread compressed 39% over the month.

For the WHY, the tracked conversation leans roughly even today — 2 neutral, 1 bearish, 1 bullish across four voices — with the bearish thread carrying the loudest signal. The dominant view attributes recent weakness to a hedge-fund liquidation event in information technology: prime-broker flow data shared in the tracked conversation flags the week ending June 25 as the largest net IT-sector sale in the dataset's history (roughly a -4 Z-score reading). The same bearish thread highlights surging cost of leveraged equity exposure (implied 3-month S&P financing cost near 110 basis points, the highest since late 2024). The bullish minority points to intraday gap-fill setups in QQQ/SPY and bouncing technicals in MU and TSLA. This sentiment narrative is consistent with the data: the underperformance of QQQ vs. Dow, the WEAK status on Technology and Nasdaq 100, and the rotation into Industrials/Financials/Healthcare all align with hedge funds unwinding tech and capital rotating toward cyclicals and defensives. The narrative and the tape agree.

Underneath the index level, the rotation is doing real work. Six of eleven GICS sectors are HOT (Industrials, Financials, Healthcare, Utilities, Consumer Staples, plus the Russell 2000) with bullish MACD and RSIs in the high-50s to low-70s. Technology and Communication Services are WEAK with bearish MACD. Energy and Materials are outright bearish — consistent with the commodity unwind. This is a textbook defensive-and-cyclical rotation away from mega-cap tech, and the Early-Runway radar is lighting up exactly where the strength is: Travel Services, Diagnostics & Research, Credit Services, and Specialty Pharma all flag as validated rotation tailwinds early in their hot spells.

Forward watch: the bounce is real but momentum hasn't confirmed (MACD still below signal on SPY/QQQ). If VIX rolls back under 17 and MACD crosses up, this becomes a re-engagement signal. If VIX pushes through 20 with another tech-led leg lower, the financing-cost stress narrative gets validated and risk should be trimmed. For now, the rotation is the trade — hunt longs in the HOT sectors and Early-Runway industries, not in the broad index.
